children: Netflix (NFLX) shares slid about 5% on Friday after Wells Fargo turned more cautious on the streaming giant, lowering its rating to Underweight and cutting its price target to $57 from $80.

The firm said changing viewing patterns and uncertainty around Netflix's content pipeline prompted the downgrade. Based on the new target, Wells Fargo sees the stock trading well below its most recent closing level.

Analysts estimated overall viewing activity on Netflix declined 8% year over year during the first six months of 2026. They also noted that engagement with the company's leading original productions weakened and could deteriorate further during the remainder of the year.

The report said Netflix has broadened its entertainment offerings through categories such as sports, gaming and documentaries, while increasing its presence on external platforms including Alphabet-owned YouTube (GOOG). Wells Fargo said that approach may expand reach but could alter the balance between broad engagement and blockbuster original programming.

The brokerage also trimmed its profitability forecasts for 2027 and 2028, citing expectations for higher content-related pressure. Analysts said investors may face greater uncertainty around future earnings trends as Netflix evaluates its spending priorities and programming strategy.

title: Wells Fargo Sends Stark Warning on Netflix Stock -- Sees 24% Downside
